scope: 10 canyon and sanctuary surface terrain plates; replacement art only, no gameplay code, collision, topology, camera or props changes by this art task.
authoring: Original raster artwork and all visual repairs created with built-in image_gen. Existing game maps and exact terrain guides used as edit references. Diagnostic overlays are analysis artifacts only, not game assets.
registration: Existing Tools/art/upscale_surface.py: local Real-ESRGAN x4plus, then exact world-size × 48 pixels registration. Upscaling does not create a new layout or prove geometric correspondence; in-game sampling remains Point.

references.type: official text and linked environment images
references.use: shared architectural axes and repeated masonry scale across foreground and surroundings; no copied assets
broad terraced sediment strata and subdued depth, not original artwork
continuous weathered stone and submerged ruins, no asset reproduction

researchLimitation: Web page text and image-search descriptions accessed; local project inputs/outputs directly visually inspected. Browser surfaces unavailable, so no claim of independent full-resolution browser inspection of remote screenshots.
artDirection: A shared high-oblique game projection. Use blocked exterior space for sloping, rounded support masses instead of following tile stairs as upright square cliffs. Keep functional paths dry and clear; curve supporting geology and submerged stone on the blocked side. Existing separate landmarks remain in game.

qa.type: Offline image/material screening plus visual inspection; parent performs actual native runtime verification. This screening is not a collision test.
qa.heuristic: Teal/green-blue pixels on the guide land mask, chamfer distance from the mask edge; examine new samples deeper than 0.5 tile. Wet stone, dark cracks and subpixel boundaries can yield false positives.
qa.legacySunkenGuideNote: 16 pre-existing color samples remain unchanged in the main sanctuary; the earlier guide/feet-mask review identified its narrow disconnected guide strip as non-walkable actual water. No new ground was invented to cover it.
qa.limitation: Small boundary details below the half-tile screening threshold are not certified by the color test; actual runtime scene, props and feet alignment must be reviewed separately. Existing authored straight bridges, rectangular pool sides and blocked interior ribs are retained where required by unchanged topology.

assets.improvement: Broad rounded sandstone shoulders, tapered buttresses, continuous sediment planes, subdued lower ravine; existing bridge/stair and pond locations retained.
Curved eroded pond banks and sloping outer strata replace sharp cliff blocks; precise small dry-floor repair at two shore samples.
Quarry floor uses small fractures and sediment rather than cobble noise. Interior blocked ribs taper into talus and outer corners use wider stratum shoulders.
Wind-worn wedge buttresses and rounded eroded shelves give coherent foreground support, with contrast reduced across distant ravine.
Blocked rock ribs have eroded tapered flanks and rounded toes. Warm terrain scale and strata match adjacent canyon maps.

Large slanted enclosing rock masses and worn olive limestone replace repeated rectangular upright walls. Upper pond, center asymmetric water and lower altar footprint preserved; existing runtime arch/altar remain separate.
Smaller worn limestone and soil infill, rounded dry shore shoulders, submerged supports outside floor. Broad contiguous dry perimeter repair eliminates water-colored notches within walkable land.
Broken polygon outer shoulders and small paving scale replace oversized slab islands. Northeast and southeast dry bank extended to the authored land boundary.
Irregular limestone/soil surface, curved ruined shoulders and pale dry margins backed by olive submerged masonry; repaired western and lower banks.

Continuous rounded dry stone rim and weathered circular masonry retain the court topology. All inner and outer wet seams remain outside the required dry floor, with final local northeast arc correction.

prompts.sunken_sanctum:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is existing high-oblique orthographic RPG terrain to redesign. Image2 exact floor/water mask (tan floor, blue water, dark rock; brown tiny spots are runtime props, keep ground). Preserve image registration, each passage and all safe tan walking areas. Preserve water footprint and depth cues. No new actors, trees, buildings, columns, statues, altars, UI or text: major architectures/props are separate runtime layers. Produce original refined pixel-art game terrain with coherent camera axes and small-character scale, not a large tabletop illustration.
Replace repetitive giant jigsaw slab tiles with weathered smaller limestone paving remnants partly buried in silty earth, broad quiet worn surfaces, occasional aligned architectural courses that explain the old structure; use purposeful cracks, not identical repeated motifs. Overall muted sage-gray stone, warm pale upper faces, olive moss, deep green water. Upper-left light with grounded shadow. Surrounding blocked rock and masonry must connect structurally with playable floor rather than form a rectangular black frame.
CRITICAL: remove 90-degree cardboard-cutout shorelines and uniform curb-bead borders. Keep every navigable foot position, but use existing water/blocked area just outside the edge to add smooth sweeping shallow submerged broken slabs, polygonal collapsed footing fans and tapered stepped masonry, clearly UNDER WATER or SLOPING. Never create apparent passable bridges or cover genuine water with dry floor. Every wet transition follows the same stone direction/scale as dry floor. Curved submerged depth contours and asymmetrical fractured wedges soften grid corners; no encroaching water into safe floor. Outer water pool corners blend into dark sloping rock rubble so no rectangular aquarium border. Crisp fine pixel texture with reduced noise, no blur or huge fog, no neon waterline. Tall2:3map: preserve north upper pool with central stairs, broad center-left floor, long middle-right pond, thin center-bottom neck and circular lower altar foundation exactly. The upper northern dark zone is reserved for runtime huge arch and waterfall; leave it dark supporting natural rock, DO NOT paint a second arch. The lower circular island is reserved for runtime altar; keep it simple worn flush radial masonry without new altar. Major improvement: replace the wallpaper of same upright rock rectangles across whole background with broad slanted fractured damp limestone masses and a few broken buttress foundation seams integrated along both sides. High dark sidewall strata curve around the floor and shoreline; avoid overpowering the existing architecture. Make the central illuminated floor and lower island visually belong to one flooded ruin and keep the narrow neck unobstructed.
